title: Thanksgiving for the end of idolatry and the proclamation of the consubstantial Trinity
english: We give thanks to God, most mighty emperor, for he steers for you the earthly kingdom. Through you he abolished the error of idols, and he established the cheerful confidence of the faithful in boldness. The savor of demons has ceased. The objects of worship of Greek polytheism have been destroyed. The darkness of ignorance is driven away. The whole world is illumined by the light of the knowledge of God. The Father is glorified. The Son is worshiped together with him. The Holy Spirit is proclaimed. The consubstantial Trinity is preached: one Godhead in three persons and subsistences.
translator_notes: Copy-text PG 18 Khazarzar Allocutio ad Constantinum [Sp.]. PD.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
Attributed Eustathius; PG marks Spurious — disclosed in About.
orientation: Eustathius opens his address by thanking God before the emperor for abolishing idolatry through him and for the freedom now given to the faithful.
